sections.overview: Pseudogobiopsis tigrellus is a tiny freshwater goby known from the Mamberamo River system of western New Guinea.
sections.identification: It is a small, slender goby reaching about two point three centimetres standard length. The original description placed it in Gobius as Gobius tigrellus.
sections.habitat: Records describe it in shallow marginal pools away from the main current, over sand or rock, in freshwater.
sections.diet: The sources consulted do not report prey or a species-specific diet.
sections.behavior: Field records found individuals alone or in loose groups of a few fish, usually resting on the bottom.
sections.reproduction: The references reviewed provide no specific information on its reproduction.
sections.ecology: Only a small number of old specimens and localities are reported, so its wider distribution and ecology remain poorly known.
sections.conservation: The latest FishBase-linked IUCN assessment classifies it as Data Deficient, reflecting the limited available information.
